title: 11+ Vocabulary: How to Build Words That Stick
description: Vocabulary improves most when children meet, use and revisit words repeatedly. Long word lists can create the appearance of learning without building reliable recall.

children: Vocabulary improves most when children meet, use and revisit words repeatedly. Long word lists can create the appearance of learning without building reliable recall.
Group words by meaning, topic, prefix, suffix or contrast. For example, learning reluctant alongside hesitant, unwilling and eager creates useful connections and makes distinctions clearer.

Ask the child to say and write an original sentence using the new word. Then change the context and use it again. If a word only exists on a flashcard, it is less likely to transfer into comprehension or writing.
Review after a day, a few days and then a week. Quick retrieval is more useful than rereading. Ask for the meaning, a synonym, an antonym and a sentence.
For 11+ preparation, vocabulary should support comprehension and reasoning rather than become an isolated memory exercise. Ten well-learned words are more valuable than fifty half-remembered ones.
